How Many Different Chinese Dialects ? Look at here

These Chinese dialects are all about pronunciation; The Chinese literature is consistent. Mandarin Chinese is the "official Chinese". The pronunciation is based on Northern Chinese dialects. Generally, majority Chinese can speak Mandarin, while many have their own dialects which they prefer to use when they talk to "hometown-people"; many Chinese also have unique accents, depending where they are from.

I stumbled across this recently and it totally blew my mind. I thought there were only two dialects of Chinese, and that they were mutually indistinguishable. To discover that there are so many more just made me feel sorry for Chinese people. I live in the US and I can understand people from every part of it, its neighbor Canada, and many other places around the world where English is taught.

Yes. That is why Chinese have to learn Mandarin to communicate with each other. For example, I am from Liaoning province. My dialect is very similar to Mandarin, only with a funny accent and some funky idioms. If people are speaking, such as Cantonese, Shanghainese, Fuzhounese, Fujianese to me, they just sounds like foreign languages. There is no way for me to understand. Let alone people from Tibet ( Tibetan), XInjiang (Uyghur), Inner Mongolia(Mongolian) and the city of Yanbian (Korean) are speaking authentic foreign languages. I went to college in the City of Shanghai, two of my roommates speak Shanghainese, another one speaks Korean (from the city of Yanbian). The first day I though I was leaving with 3 foreign students.

That's what I thought. I once considered learning Chinese, but I'm not going to bother, because chances are I wouldn't be able to use it anyway. I just can't imagine so many foreign languages in my own country. Interpreting must be a promising career.

You are right. Unless you are interested in Chinese Culture, working in China or Chinese Classics, it is a waste of time to learn Chinese.
Interpreting is not that promising, since people speak Mandarin in official occasions, such as: government, school, company and supermarkets. Chinese people have to learn Mandarin at School.
